proposals: PPAC should publish a single annual table of India’s actual natural gas consumption by sector, in MMSCMD, back to 2012–13, so that the 2013 report’s sector-by-sector projections for power, fertiliser, city gas and industry can be checked line by line rather than against scattered trade-press figures.

PNGRB should publish a forecast-versus-actual review of every demand projection it has received or commissioned, starting with the 2013 Vision 2030 report, so that the gap between 571 MMSCMD projected and roughly 188 MMSCMD consumed in 2023–24 is documented by the regulator itself.

PNGRB should require pipeline authorisation applications to state the demand forecast relied on and report utilisation against it every year after commissioning, so that a grid built for demand near 600–750 MMSCMD but running at around 50% utilisation is visible line by line.

The Petroleum Ministry and PNGRB should publish gas-pipeline lengths, operational and authorised, in a dated official table every year, so that figures such as 25,400 km operational and 34,200 km authorised do not have to be reconstructed from year-end press reviews.
